Order 
Case diary is perused.

This is the second application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of BNSS/439 of Cr.P.C. for grant of bail relating to Crime No.551 of 2024 registered at Police Station - Kotwali, District - Datia (M.P.) for the offence under Sections 420, 409, 467, 468 & 478 of IPC.

As per the prosecution case, on 20.04.2024, an authorized officer of Kotak Mahindra Bank, Mr.
Amit Gurjar, submitted a complaint at Police Station Kotwali stating that the bank employee/applicant-accused had misappropriated an amount of Rs.1,38,335/-, which was collected from customers in the form of loan installments and was not deposited into the bank.
It was alleged that the accused fraudulently retained the said amount.

Upon investigation conducted by Sub-Inspector Amit Kumar Osare of Police Station Kotwali, it was found that the applicant/accused had indeed NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:17111 2 MCRC-22246-2025 committed the said fraud.
On the basis of such allegation, the above crime was registered.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case due to internal administrative issues within the bank.

The applicant was working as a collection executive for Kotak Mahindra Bank and was responsible for collecting loan installments Gaurav Rajput vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171739314/

sentences.text: It is submitted that due to certain clerical lapses and procedural delays, the collected amount could not be deposited within the prescribed time, which led to the present complaint being lodged against the applicant.
It is further submitted that the applicant has no criminal antecedents and is a law-abiding citizen.
He has cooperated fully with the investigation and is not a flight risk.
It is further submitted that the alleged amount of Rs.1,38,335/- has already been paid and there is no financial loss caused to the bank at present.
Counsel further contends that the offence is triable by a Magistrate and does not involve any exceptional circumstances justifying denial of bail.
The applicant undertakes to abide by all the conditions that may be imposed by this Hon'ble Court and shall be available for investigation or trial as and when required.
The applicant is in custody since 20.07.2024 .
In light of the above submissions, it is prayed that the applicant be released on bail.

Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor for the State opposed the application and prayed for its rejection by contending that on the basis of the allegations and the material available on record, no case for grant of bail is made out.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:17111 3 MCRC-22246-2025

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the nature of the offence, the fact that the alleged amount has been paid,
and without commenting on the merits of the case, the court deems it appropriate to grant bail to the applicant.
Accordingly, the bail application filed under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant shall be released on bail upon his furnishing a personal bond of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand only) with one solvent surety of like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, subject to the following conditions:
The applicant shall not tamper with the evidence or influence witnesses in any manner.
He shall appear before the trial Court on all dates fixed, without fail.
He shall not leave India without prior permission of the trial Court.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the prosecution shall be at liberty to move for cancellation of bail.
Application stands disposed of.
CC as per Rules.
